argv: You are the Claude side of an OAC live test, nonce 37e28354. Do these steps in order. Step 1: call the whoami tool of the oac MCP server and print one line: CLAUDE-SID-37e28354: followed by the session_id it returned. Step 2: run the Bash command sleep 10 again and again, at most 60 times, stopping as soon as a channel message from another OAC session has reached you (use Start-Sleep 10 if you have no Bash tool). Whenever a channel message reaches you, at any step, print one line that starts with RECEIVED-37e28354: then its text, then a vertical bar, then its oac_sender, then a vertical bar, then its oac_message_id, all on one line. Never reply to a message. Step 3: call the send tool of the oac MCP server three times, to the session <SESSION_ID>, each time with one text part, in this order. Text 1: G8LIVE 37e28354 T1 Hello from Claude, hand-off one. Text 2: G8LIVE 37e28354 T2 Hello from Claude, hand-off two. Text 3: G8LIVE 37e28354 T3 Please answer this message with the OAC reply tool, naming this message in in_reply_to. After each send print one line: SENT-37e28354-N: followed by the id the send result returned, where N is 1, 2 or 3. Step 4: run sleep 10 again and again, at most 60 times, stopping once three more channel messages have reached you. Step 5: print the line CLAUDE-DONE-37e28354.

holders: the shared Codex app-server daemon (left running; the driver never stops it) may hold the directory of a thread it loaded under scratch; it is released on `codex app-server daemon stop`, or when the daemon unloads the thread (documented: no subscribers and no thread activity for 30 minutes). The driver does not call thread/archive or thread/delete, which would unload it sooner, because both write to the operator's Codex thread store (thread/delete destroys the run's rollout) and whether their shutdown releases the directory handle is unverified
